test: New York State DMV Written (Knowledge) Test — Class D / DJ Learner Permit
edition: Based on the New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21), PDF at dmv.ny.gov/brochure/mv21.pdf (file dated April 20, 2026), and the online manual/DMV web pages checked October 2026

exam.rules: New York's written permit test (for Class D, DJ, M, MJ and E applicants) has 20 multiple-choice questions on rules of the road, safe driving, road signs, and alcohol/drug laws. To pass you must answer at least 14 of the 20 correctly AND at least 2 of the 4 road-sign questions — missing 3 or 4 sign questions fails the test even if your total is 14 or higher. The same test applies to adults and teens; you must be at least 16 to get a learner permit, and you also take a vision test (20/40 in at least one eye). The test is taken at a DMV office on a touch screen or paper in 20 languages; applicants under 18 can take it online (then must wait 3 business days before visiting an office), and high-school students from age 15 years 11 months may take it at participating schools (OKTA).

questions.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a New York learner permit?
questions.explain: New York issues learner permits starting at age 16; people under 16 may not drive in the state even with an out-of-state licence.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Driver Licenses'

questions.q: On the New York written permit test, how many of the 20 questions must you answer correctly to pass?
questions.explain: You need 14 of 20 correct overall, plus at least 2 of the 4 road-sign questions.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Vision and Knowledge Tests'

questions.q: The New York written test includes 4 road-sign questions. What is the rule for them?
options: They are practice items and do not count
You must answer at least 2 of the 4 correctly, or you fail
They only count if your overall score is below 14
questions.explain: Even with 14 or more correct overall, you fail unless at least 2 of the 4 road-sign questions are right.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Vision and Knowledge Tests'

questions.q: What vision standard must you meet to pass the DMV vision test?
options: 20/40 in at least one eye, with or without corrective lenses
questions.explain: The manual requires 20/40 vision in at least one eye; glasses or contacts may be used.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Vision and Knowledge Tests'

questions.q: Who may supervise a learner permit holder who is practicing driving (outside the special NYC and Long Island rules)?
options: A driver age 21 or older licensed for the vehicle, seated in the front seat
Any licensed driver age 18 or older, seated anywhere
Any adult passenger age 25 or older, licensed or not
A licensed driver age 19 or older in the back seat
questions.explain: The supervising driver must be at least 21, hold a licence valid for that vehicle, and sit in the front seat.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'The Learner Permit'

questions.q: Before a road test, your parent or guardian must certify (form MV-262) that you completed how much supervised practice?
options: At least 30 hours, including 10 at night
At least 50 hours, including at least 15 after sunset
At least 40 hours, including 5 at night
At least 65 hours, including 10 in bad weather
questions.explain: Form MV-262 certifies at least 50 hours of practice, with at least 15 of them after sunset.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'For Junior Drivers with Permits'

questions.q: How long must a junior learner permit be held before a road test can be scheduled?
questions.explain: A junior permit must be held for at least six months (not counting any time it was suspended or revoked) before the road test.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Special Rules for Drivers with Junior Permits and Licenses'

questions.q: How long is the pre-licensing course that most new drivers must complete before booking a road test?
questions.explain: Most applicants must complete an approved 5-hour Pre-Licensing Course (or a driver education course) before the road test.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'When You Apply for Your First License'

questions.q: If you hold a junior learner permit, who is the only person allowed to sit in the front seat with you?
options: An immediate family member of any age
questions.explain: With a junior permit, the only front-seat passenger allowed is the supervising driver.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Driving with a Junior Learner Permit'

questions.q: With a junior license (Class DJ), how many passengers under age 21 may you carry (unless they are immediate family)?
questions.explain: A junior licence holder may not carry more than one passenger under 21 unless they are members of the driver's immediate family.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Junior Operator Restrictions'

questions.q: With a junior license (Class DJ), when may you drive in New York City (the five boroughs)?
options: Only with a parent in the car
Never — junior license holders may not drive there
Any time, if you hold a driver education certificate
questions.explain: The regional chart shows junior licence holders must not drive in New York City at any hour.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Regional Restrictions for a Junior License'

questions.q: With a junior learner permit in New York City, what is required to practice between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.?
options: Any licensed driver over 18 and an ordinary car
A supervisor age 25 or older; dual controls are optional
No practice is ever allowed in New York City
A qualified supervisor (parent, guardian, driving instructor, etc.) and a vehicle with dual controls
questions.explain: In the five boroughs a junior permit holder may practice 5 a.m.–9 p.m. only with a listed supervisor (age 21+) in a vehicle with dual controls (dual brakes).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit'

questions.q: Upstate (outside NYC and Long Island), a junior learner permit holder may practice between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m. only when supervised by whom?
options: A parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, driver education teacher or driving school instructor (age 21+)
Any licensed driver age 18 or older
Any licensed driver age 21 or older
No one — night driving is banned upstate
questions.explain: Upstate night practice requires a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis, driver education teacher or driving school instructor who is 21+ and properly licensed.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit'

questions.q: Upstate, between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m., a junior license (Class DJ) holder may:
options: Drive only to and from school
Drive only with a parent in the car
questions.explain: In upstate counties a junior licence holder may drive unaccompanied between 5 a.m. and 9 p.m.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Regional Restrictions for a Junior License'

questions.q: A learner permit holder may NOT practice driving in which of these places?
options: On a residential street in Albany
On a two-lane rural road upstate
On the Taconic State Parkway in Westchester County
In an empty shopping-center parking lot open to the public
questions.explain: Permit holders may not drive on the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River or Taconic State parkways in Westchester, in DMV road test areas, on NYC park streets, or on TBTA bridges and tunnels.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'General Rules for All Drivers with Learner Permits'

questions.q: A junior permit or junior license holder is convicted of a texting or hand-held phone violation. What happens?
options: Two points only, with no suspension
The permit or license is suspended for 120 days
questions.explain: Junior permits/licences (and probationary licences) are suspended for 120 days for a first texting or cell phone conviction.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Special Rules for Drivers with Junior Permits and Licenses'

questions.q: A junior permit or license holder is convicted of one serious traffic violation (3 or more points). What is the penalty?
questions.explain: One serious violation (3+ points) or two other violations leads to a 60-day suspension for junior drivers.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Special Rules for Drivers with Junior Permits and Licenses'

questions.q: A driver who is 18 or older passes the road test. For how long is the new license on probation?
questions.explain: New drivers licensed at 18 or older are on probation for six months.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Probation Period for All Other Newly Licensed Drivers'

questions.q: During the probation period, a conviction for speeding, reckless driving, following too closely or DWAI results in:
options: A 60-day suspension, followed by a new six-month probation
Five extra points but no suspension
questions.explain: Any of those convictions (or any two violations) on probation brings a 60-day suspension and then a fresh six-month probation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Probation Period for All Other Newly Licensed Drivers'

questions.q: After moving, how soon must you notify the DMV of your new address?
questions.explain: Address changes must be reported to the DMV within 10 days (form MV-232 or online).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 1, 'Change of Address'

questions.q: How many points within 24 months can lead to the suspension of your New York license?
questions.explain: The DMV suspends a licence when a driver gets 11 or more points within 24 months.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'The Point System'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 11 to 20 mph over the posted limit?
questions.explain: Speeding 11–20 mph over carries 4 points (1–10 mph = 3, 21–30 = 6, 31–40 = 8, over 40 = 11).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'The Point System'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for passing a stopped school bus?
questions.explain: Failing to stop for a school bus carries 8 points under the current point schedule.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'The Point System'

questions.q: How many points does a conviction for using a hand-held phone or texting while driving add to your record?
questions.explain: Improper cell phone use and texting each carry 5 points.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'The Point System'

questions.q: Completing a DMV-approved crash prevention (PIRP) course can reduce your point total by up to how many points?
questions.explain: PIRP can reduce up to 4 points and cut liability/collision premiums by at least 10% for three years; it cannot prevent a mandatory suspension.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'The Point System'

questions.q: If you get 6 points within 18 months, what Driver Responsibility Assessment must you pay?
options: $100 per year for three years, plus $25 per extra point per year
Nothing, as long as you take a PIRP course
questions.explain: Six points in 18 months triggers $100 a year for three years, plus $25 per additional point each year; PIRP does not reduce it.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Driver Responsibility Assessments'

questions.q: What happens if you drive, or let someone else drive, your uninsured vehicle in New York?
options: Your license is suspended for 30 days
Your license is revoked for at least one year
questions.explain: Driving or allowing operation of an uninsured vehicle leads to revocation of at least one year.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'No Insurance'

questions.q: What is the minimum liability coverage New York requires for property damage in one incident?
questions.explain: Minimum coverage includes $10,000 for property damage ($25,000/$50,000 injury; $50,000/$100,000 death).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 3, 'Insurance'

questions.q: In New York, a blood alcohol content (BAC) of .08 percent or higher is evidence of:
options: Nothing, unless you fail a road-side test
questions.explain: BAC of .08 or more is evidence of intoxication; more than .05 is evidence of impairment; .18 or more is aggravated DWI.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Alcohol, Other Drugs and the Law'

questions.q: A BAC of more than what level is legal evidence that your ability to drive is impaired (DWAI)?
questions.explain: More than .05 BAC is legal evidence of impairment (DWAI).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Alcohol, Other Drugs and the Law'

questions.q: Aggravated driving while intoxicated (Agg-DWI) applies at a BAC of:
questions.explain: A BAC of .18 or higher is evidence of aggravated DWI.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Alcohol, Other Drugs and the Law'

questions.q: Under New York's Zero Tolerance Law, a driver under 21 found with a BAC of .02 to .07 will have their license:
questions.explain: Zero Tolerance: a BAC of .02–.07 under 21 brings a six-month suspension after a DMV hearing.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Zero Tolerance for Drivers Under Age 21'

questions.q: To be re-licensed after a Zero Tolerance suspension, an under-21 driver must pay:
options: A $125 civil penalty and a $100 suspension termination fee
questions.explain: The driver must pay a $125 civil penalty plus a $100 suspension termination fee.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Zero Tolerance for Drivers Under Age 21'

questions.q: What is the penalty for a second Zero Tolerance violation?
options: Revocation for at least one year or until age 21, whichever is longer
questions.explain: A second Zero Tolerance violation brings revocation for at least one year or until age 21, whichever is longer.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Zero Tolerance for Drivers Under Age 21'

questions.q: What does New York's Implied Consent law mean?
options: You may refuse a chemical test with no penalty
Police need a court order before any breath test
By driving in New York, you are considered to have agreed to a chemical test if arrested for an alcohol or drug offense
Only commercial drivers must take chemical tests
questions.explain: Driving in New York means you have consented to a chemical test (breath, blood, urine or saliva) if arrested for an alcohol/drug violation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Chemical Tests'

questions.q: A driver age 21 or older refuses a chemical test (first refusal). What is the license penalty?
options: No penalty if found not guilty of DWI
Revocation for at least one year
questions.explain: A chemical test refusal by a driver over 21 results in a minimum one-year revocation (plus a $500 civil penalty).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Chemical Test Refusals'

questions.q: What civil penalty must you pay after a chemical test refusal revocation (non-commercial driver, first refusal)?
questions.explain: A chemical test refusal carries a $500 civil penalty ($750 if within five years of an earlier alcohol/drug/refusal revocation).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Fees and Civil Penalties'

questions.q: If a DMV hearing confirms you refused a chemical test, but the court finds you not guilty of DWI:
options: Your license is still revoked for the refusal
Your license is suspended for 10 days
questions.explain: Refusal is a separate matter; the licence is revoked even if you are acquitted of the alcohol/drug charge.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Chemical Tests'

questions.q: Can you be convicted of DWI without a chemical test result?
options: No, a breath or blood test is always required
Only if you were in a crash
Yes — the officer's testimony about your driving, appearance and behavior can be enough
Only if you admit to drinking
questions.explain: Officer testimony about your driving and behavior can provide enough evidence to convict, even without a chemical test.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Alcohol, Other Drugs and the Law'

questions.q: Which of these drinks contains the most alcohol: 1½ oz of 80-proof liquor, 5 oz of wine, 12 oz of beer, or 12 oz of wine cooler?
options: They all contain about the same amount
questions.explain: Each of these standard drinks contains about the same amount of alcohol; none is 'safer' than the others.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Your BAC'

questions.q: For a 150-pound man, one standard drink raises BAC by about how much?
questions.explain: Each standard drink raises a 150-lb male's BAC by roughly .02 percent.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Your BAC'

questions.q: On average, how long does it take the body to remove the alcohol in one 12-oz beer?
questions.explain: On average it takes about one hour for the body to eliminate the alcohol from one standard drink.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Your BAC'

questions.q: What is the only effective way to lower your BAC?
options: Wait — time is the only thing that works
questions.explain: Coffee, exercise and cold showers do not lower BAC; only time does.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Your BAC'

questions.q: Your BAC depends on which three factors?
options: The type of drink, your fitness, and your mood
The brand of drink, the temperature, and your height
How well you 'hold your liquor', your age, and the time of day
How much you drink, the time between drinks, and your weight
questions.explain: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight — not on the type of beverage.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Your BAC'

questions.q: What is the minimum license penalty for a first DWI (.08 BAC) conviction?
options: Revocation for at least six months
Revocation for at least three years
questions.explain: A first DWI conviction brings a minimum six-month revocation, a $500–$1,000 fine, and up to one year in jail.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Penalties for Alcohol/Drug Related Violations'

questions.q: What is the minimum license penalty for a first Aggravated DWI (BAC .18 or higher) conviction?
options: Revocation for at least six months
Revocation for at least one year
questions.explain: First-offense Agg-DWI carries a minimum one-year revocation and a $1,000–$2,500 fine.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Penalties for Alcohol/Drug Related Violations'

questions.q: What is the license penalty for a first DWAI (alcohol) conviction?
questions.explain: A first DWAI-alcohol conviction (a traffic infraction) brings a 90-day suspension and a $300–$500 fine.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Penalties for Alcohol/Drug Related Violations'

questions.q: Under Leandra's Law, driving while intoxicated with a child under what age in the vehicle can be charged as a felony?
questions.explain: Leandra's Law makes it a class E felony to drive drunk with a child under 16 in the vehicle.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'The Ignition Interlock Program and Leandra's Law'

questions.q: After a DWI conviction, the court must order an ignition interlock device installed on vehicles you own or operate for at least:
questions.explain: Courts must order an interlock for at least 12 months (it can be waived after six months in some cases).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'The Ignition Interlock Program and Leandra's Law'

questions.q: If you are convicted of DWI, in addition to fines you must pay a Driver Responsibility Assessment of:
questions.explain: Alcohol/drug convictions and chemical test refusals carry a $250-per-year assessment for three years.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Driver Responsibility Assessments'

questions.q: If you are under 21 when arrested and convicted of an alcohol- or drug-related driving violation, the minimum revocation is:
questions.explain: Drivers under 21 face at least a one-year revocation for alcohol/drug driving convictions.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Drivers Under Age 21'

questions.q: Under New York's open container law, which of these is a traffic infraction on a public road?
options: A passenger in a licensed stretch limousine drinking wine
Carrying a sealed bottle of wine in the trunk
Having drunk a beer two hours before driving
A passenger drinking an alcoholic beverage in a regular passenger car
questions.explain: Drivers and passengers may not drink or have an open alcoholic container in a vehicle on a public road; passengers in vehicles like licensed limousines are exempt.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Open Container Law'

questions.q: Why is drinking and driving especially dangerous at night?
options: Alcohol reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and vision is already limited at night
Alcohol improves night vision only briefly
Alcohol has a stronger effect on your BAC after dark
questions.explain: Night vision is already restricted, and alcohol slows recovery from the glare of oncoming headlights.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'What Alcohol Does'

questions.q: Which of these can lead to a charge of driving while ability impaired?
options: Driving impaired by alcohol, cannabis, illegal drugs, some prescription drugs, or a combination
questions.explain: It can be a criminal offense to drive impaired by alcohol, drugs (including cannabis and some prescription drugs), or a combination.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 9, 'Other Drugs'

questions.q: A driver over 21 refuses a chemical test within five years of a prior refusal or alcohol/drug-related violation. The minimum revocation is:
questions.explain: A repeat refusal within five years (over 21) brings a minimum 18-month revocation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 2, 'Chemical Test Refusals'

questions.q: Your light is green, but a car is already in the intersection turning left in front of you. What should you do?
options: Go, because you have a green light
Let it finish its turn before you enter
questions.explain: A driver approaching an intersection must yield to traffic already in the intersection.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You and an oncoming driver reach an intersection at about the same time. You want to turn left; the other driver is going straight. Who must yield?
options: You must yield to the oncoming driver
The oncoming driver must yield to you
Whoever is driving the larger vehicle
questions.explain: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: At an intersection with no signs or signals, two cars arrive at the same time from roads at right angles. Who must yield?
options: The driver on the right yields to the driver on the left
The driver on the left yields to the driver on the right
Whoever reaches the center line first goes
questions.explain: At uncontrolled intersections (and when two drivers stop at stop signs at the same time at right angles), the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You are stopped at a stop sign planning to go straight. A driver on the cross street to your right stopped at the same time and is also going straight. What should you do?
options: Go first because you are going straight
Go first because the other driver must yield to the left
Yield to the driver on your right
Wave the driver on your left through
questions.explain: When drivers stop at the same time at right angles, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You are leaving a parking lot and entering a street. What must you do?
options: Enter quickly and merge with traffic
Yield only to vehicles coming from the right
Sound your horn and pull out
Stop and yield to traffic on the street and to pedestrians
questions.explain: A vehicle entering a roadway from a driveway, private road or other non-roadway must stop and yield to roadway traffic and pedestrians.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You are stopped at a red light. A pedestrian starts across in front of you, and then your light turns green. What should you do?
options: Wait until the pedestrian has crossed
Go, since you now have a green light
questions.explain: You must let a pedestrian who is lawfully in the crosswalk finish crossing.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: Your light is green, but traffic is backed up on the far side of the intersection so you cannot get all the way through. What should you do?
options: Enter the intersection and wait there
Wait before the intersection until there is room to clear it
Go, because you have the right of way
questions.explain: You may not enter an intersection if you cannot get completely through it; blocking it can cause gridlock.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: When approaching a traffic circle or rotary, who has the right of way?
questions.explain: Drivers approaching a traffic circle or rotary must yield to drivers already in it.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: You hear a siren and see an ambulance approaching from behind with flashing lights. What must you do?
options: Speed up to stay ahead of it
Pull over to the left shoulder
Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explain: Yield to emergency vehicles by safely pulling to the right edge and stopping until they pass.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: You are in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches. What should you do?
options: Drive out of the intersection, then pull over to the right and stop
Stop right where you are in the intersection
Back up out of the intersection
Turn left to get out of its path
questions.explain: If you are in an intersection, clear it first, then pull over to the right and stop.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: On a two-way road, an emergency vehicle using its siren is coming toward you in the opposite lane. What does New York law require?
options: Keep driving, since it is in the other lane
Pull over to the right and stop
Stop in your lane without pulling over
questions.explain: You must pull over and stop even when the emergency vehicle is approaching in the opposite lane of a two-way road.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: You hear a siren close by but cannot tell where the emergency vehicle is. What should you do?
options: Speed up to clear the area
Pull over to the right edge and stop until you are sure it is not coming toward you
questions.explain: If you hear a siren nearby but cannot locate it, safely pull over to the right and stop until you know it is not heading your way.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Emergency Vehicles'

questions.q: A personal car showing a flashing blue light is approaching. Who is likely driving it?
options: A volunteer firefighter responding to an alarm
questions.explain: Volunteer firefighters may show blue lights; volunteer ambulance/rescue members show green lights. These are not authorized emergency vehicles.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Blue, Green and Amber Lights'

questions.q: Under New York's Move Over Law, what must you do when passing a stopped police car, tow truck or other hazard vehicle with its lights flashing on the shoulder?
options: Slow down on any road, and on multi-lane controlled-access highways move out of the adjacent lane if safe
Only move over if a police officer signals
Nothing, as long as you stay in your lane
questions.explain: Drivers must reduce speed on all roads and, on parkways/interstates/controlled-access roads with multiple lanes, move out of the lane next to the vehicle unless unsafe.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: On a parkway or controlled-access highway, the Move Over Law also applies when passing:

Only vehicles in the travel lane
questions.explain: New York extended the Move Over Law to any vehicle stopped on the shoulder or roadway of a parkway or controlled-access highway.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Move Over Law'

questions.q: A pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is starting to cross at a crosswalk against the signal. What should you do?
options: Proceed, since your signal is green
Yield — blind pedestrians always have the right of way at crosswalks
questions.explain: A special law gives blind pedestrians with a guide dog or white/metal cane the right of way at marked or unmarked crosswalks, even if signals are not in their favor.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: You want to turn left into a driveway with no signs or signals. What must you do?
options: Turn immediately because driveways have priority
Yield only if the oncoming car signals
Yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard
questions.explain: For any left turn, including into a driveway or lot, you must yield to approaching traffic close enough to be a hazard.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: A steady green light means:
options: Go, but yield to other traffic and pedestrians as the law requires
Go; you always have the right of way
Speed up to beat the yellow
questions.explain: A green light allows you to go but does not remove the duty to yield to vehicles and pedestrians lawfully in the intersection.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: A stopped school bus is flashing its red lights. When must you stop?
options: Only when you are behind it
Whenever you approach it from either direction
questions.explain: Traffic from either direction must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights — on all roads, even in front of schools and in school lots.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: How far from a stopped school bus with flashing red lights should you stop?
questions.explain: You should stop at least 20 feet away from the bus.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: A school bus with flashing red lights is stopped on the other side of a divided highway. What must you do?
options: Continue, since a divider separates you
Change lanes away from the bus
questions.explain: New York requires drivers to stop for a school bus showing flashing red lights, even when the bus is across a divided highway from them.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: After stopping for a school bus, when may you proceed?
options: When the bus starts moving or the bus driver or a traffic officer signals you to go
When the children reach the sidewalk
When the yellow lights start flashing
questions.explain: Stay stopped until the bus moves again or the driver or a traffic officer waves you on.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: The yellow lights near the roof of a school bus begin to flash. What does this mean?
options: You may pass the bus quickly
The bus is about to stop to load or unload — slow down and prepare to stop
questions.explain: Flashing yellow lights warn that the bus is preparing to stop; reduce speed and be ready to stop.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: What is the minimum fine for a first conviction of passing a stopped school bus?
questions.explain: The fine ranges from at least $250 for a first violation up to $1,000 for three violations in three years (with licence revocation).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'School Buses'

questions.q: A traffic officer waves you through a red light. What should you do?
options: Wait for the light to turn green
Ignore the officer and obey the light
Follow the officer's direction and go
questions.explain: Directions from traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals and pavement markings.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Officers'

questions.q: Where must you yield to pedestrians?
options: At all crosswalks, marked or unmarked
Only at marked crosswalks with signals
Only when a crossing guard is present
questions.explain: Drivers must yield to pedestrians legally using marked or unmarked crosswalks.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Right-of-Way'

questions.q: At a modern roundabout, who has the right of way?
options: Traffic already circulating in the roundabout
questions.explain: Roundabouts use 'yield-at-entry': entering vehicles wait for a gap; circulating traffic has the right of way.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: What must you do when you see this sign?
options: Slow down and go if no one is coming
Stop only if other cars are present
Come to a full stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe
questions.explain: At a STOP sign you must stop completely before the stop line or crosswalk (or at the point nearest the intersection with a view), yield, and go when safe.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign require?
options: Come to a complete stop every time
Speed up to merge ahead of traffic
Go first; cross traffic must yield to you
Slow down and be ready to stop to let vehicles and pedestrians go first
questions.explain: At a YIELD sign, slow down, yield to traffic and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, and stop fully if necessary.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Do not enter — traffic on this road comes toward you

questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: You see this sign facing you. What does it tell you?
options: You are driving the wrong way and must turn around safely
You must stop for a train
questions.explain: A WRONG WAY sign means you have entered a road against traffic; get out of it safely.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign indicate?
options: The maximum lawful speed under ideal conditions is 55 mph
questions.explain: This is a regulatory speed limit sign. You may be ticketed for driving at a speed not reasonable for conditions even below the limit.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
questions.explain: A red circle with a slash over a symbol means that action is not allowed — here, no left turn.

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: You may not make a U-turn here
U-turns are allowed only on green

questions.q: At an intersection with this sign, your light is red. What may you do?
options: Turn right after a full stop
Wait for a green light; you may not turn on red
Turn left after a full stop
Turn if no cars are coming
questions.explain: Where NO TURN ON RED is posted, you may not turn on a red light.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign tell you?
options: Turn in the direction of the arrow now
Traffic on this road moves only in the direction of the arrow
questions.explain: A ONE WAY sign shows that traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Road divides ahead; go either way
Keep to the right of the divider or obstruction
questions.explain: This 'keep right of divider' sign means you must pass to the right of the island or obstruction.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign mean?
options: Passing other vehicles is not allowed here
questions.explain: DO NOT PASS signs mark zones where passing is prohibited.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

It only applies to trucks and buses

The road narrows to one lane for both directions
The right lane ends ahead; stay in or merge to the left

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?
options: Traffic entering from the right will be merging into your lane
A side road on the right

questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?

Lanes merge into one lane in your direction
questions.explain: 'Divided Highway Ends' means the median ends ahead and two-way traffic is no longer separated.
questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?

questions.explain: This sign warns of a traffic signal ahead that may not yet be visible.

questions.q: What does this sign indicate?
options: A playground with no children present
A school zone or school crossing — watch for children

questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about?

A regulation sign for a helicopter pad

questions.ref: NY DMV 'Road Signs You Must Know' (dmv.ny.gov) and New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What should you do when you see this orange sign?
options: Speed up to clear the work zone
Slow down and be ready to obey a person controlling traffic with a flag or sign
Ignore it if no workers are visible
Stop and wait for a police officer

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'How to Drive Safely in Work Zones'

options: Road work ahead; reduce speed — fines double for speeding in work zones
questions.explain: Orange signs mark work areas. Speeding fines double in work zones even when workers are not present.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'How to Drive Safely in Work Zones'

questions.q: What does a yellow plaque like this mean when placed under a warning sign?
options: The speed limit for trucks only
The speed limit for the rest of the highway
The recommended safe speed for the hazard ahead

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Warning Signs'

questions.q: This orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:

It is carrying an oversize load

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Slow-Moving Vehicles'

questions.q: What does this sign warn you about, and when is this hazard greatest in New York?
options: Cattle crossing — mainly at noon in summer
Deer crossing — especially at dawn and dusk in October through December
questions.explain: Deer crossing signs mark areas with many deer collisions; two-thirds of these crashes happen in October–December, mostly at dawn and dusk.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Avoid Collisions With Deer'

questions.q: What is the normal shape and color of a warning sign?
options: Yellow diamond with black letters or symbols
questions.explain: Warning signs are normally yellow and diamond-shaped with black lettering or symbols.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What color are destination signs that show direction and distance to places?
questions.explain: Destination signs are green with white letters and symbols.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Signs'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Stop, yield the right of way, and go when safe — like a STOP sign
Slow down and proceed with caution without stopping
The signal is broken; drive through
Stop and wait for a steady green

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: What does this signal mean?
options: Prepare for the light to turn red
questions.explain: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: What does a steady yellow light mean?
options: Speed up to get through the intersection
Proceed with caution; it will stay yellow
The light is about to turn red; be prepared to stop
Stop only if pedestrians are present

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: You see this signal. What may you do?
options: Turn only after a full stop
Turn in the direction of the arrow, while yielding to traffic and pedestrians as the law requires

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: Outside New York City, with no sign prohibiting it, what may you do at a steady red light?
options: Turn right after a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians
Go straight after a full stop if no one is coming
Turn left onto any road after stopping
questions.explain: Right on red is allowed after a full stop and yielding, unless prohibited. In NYC, turns on red are not allowed unless a sign permits it.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: In New York City, may you turn right on a red light?
options: Yes, after a full stop, anywhere
Only where a sign permits it
Yes, if no pedestrians are present
questions.explain: Turning on red is not allowed in New York City unless a sign permitting it is posted.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: When may you turn left on a steady red light in New York (outside NYC)?
options: From any road, after a full stop
From a one-way road onto another one-way road, after a full stop and yielding
Only with a green arrow showing
questions.explain: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way road into another one-way road, after stopping and yielding.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: A red arrow signal is showing for your turn lane. What may you do?
options: Turn if no traffic is coming
Do not turn in that direction until a green light or arrow appears — no turn on red
questions.explain: You may not turn in the direction of a red arrow; turns on red are not permitted at a red arrow.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: You approach an intersection where the traffic lights are not working. What must you do?
options: Stop as you would for a STOP sign, then follow right-of-way rules
Slow down and continue if clear
Go if you are on the larger road
Treat it like a flashing yellow light
questions.explain: State law requires you to stop as at a STOP sign when signals are out, unless an officer directs otherwise.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Traffic Lights'

questions.q: Above a highway lane you see a steady red 'X'. What does it mean?
options: Do not drive in this lane
This lane is for left turns only

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Lane Use Control Lights'

questions.q: A flashing yellow 'X' over a lane means:

The lane may be used only for a left turn

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Lane Use Control Lights'

Cross the center lines only to turn left into a driveway
Pass when it is safe, because the broken line is on the car's side

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: What do double solid center lines like these mean?
options: No passing or lane changes; cross only to turn left into or out of a driveway or to make a legal U-turn
Passing allowed only for slow vehicles
questions.explain: Double solid lines prohibit passing or changing lanes across them, except to turn left to enter or leave the road.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: What do these white broken lines between lanes tell you?
options: Traffic in both lanes moves in the same direction, and you may change lanes when safe
The lanes are for buses only
questions.explain: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving the same way; a broken line allows passing or lane changes when safe.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: An edge line that angles toward the center of the road means:
options: The road is getting narrower ahead
questions.explain: An edge line angling toward the center shows the road narrows ahead.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Edge and Lane Lines'

questions.q: A white diamond painted in a lane means:
options: The lane is reserved for buses, HOV car-pools, bicycles or other special vehicles
questions.explain: The diamond symbol marks reserved lanes (bus, HOV, bicycle); use them only if you meet the posted requirements.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: At an intersection with crosswalk lines but no stop line, where must you stop for a red light?
options: In the middle of the crosswalk
At the curb line of the cross street
Past the crosswalk, at the edge of the intersection
questions.explain: Stop behind the stop line when one is painted. Where there is none, stop before reaching the crosswalk.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: If no speed limit is posted, what is the maximum speed outside New York City?

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Speed'

questions.q: Unless another limit is posted, what is the speed limit in New York City?

questions.q: The speed limit on New York expressways is normally 55 mph but may be posted at what speed in some rural areas?

questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Expressway Driving'

questions.q: You are driving 50 mph in dense fog on a 55-mph expressway. Can you be ticketed?
options: Yes, for driving at a speed not reasonable for the conditions
No, you are under the limit
Only if you cause a crash
Only if the fog limit is posted
questions.explain: A police officer can ticket you for a speed that is not reasonable for conditions, even below the posted limit.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Speed'

questions.q: What is the purpose of a minimum speed limit on some highways?
options: To keep traffic flowing smoothly, since driving too slowly can be dangerous
questions.explain: Driving slower than the minimum interferes with traffic flow and creates danger.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Speed'

questions.q: To keep a safe following distance in good conditions, New York recommends at least a:
options: One car length for each 20 mph
questions.explain: Use the two-second rule: pick a fixed object and count 'one thousand one, one thousand two' after the car ahead passes it.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Allow Yourself Space'

questions.q: In bad weather or when following a large truck, your following distance should be increased to at least:
questions.explain: Increase the count to at least three or four seconds in bad weather and behind large trucks.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Allow Yourself Space'

questions.q: About how many of every 10 crashes involve rear-end collisions, usually from tailgating?

questions.q: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?
options: Move to another lane if possible, or slow down and pull off to let them pass
Hold your position and ignore them
questions.explain: Change lanes or reduce speed and pull off to let the driver go by; do not brake suddenly, which could provoke road rage.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Allow Yourself Space'

questions.q: What happens to speeding fines in a highway work zone?

They are the same as anywhere else
They double, even when workers are not present
questions.explain: Speeding fines double in work zones even when workers or work vehicles are not there.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'How to Drive Safely in Work Zones'

questions.q: How many points are assessed for speeding 1 to 10 mph over the limit?

questions.q: Your headlights light up about 350 feet ahead. 'Driving within the range of your headlights' means:

Driving at a speed that lets you stop within the distance you can see
