Slowly, matching the flow of traffic and the conditions
10 mph above the flow of traffic
questions.explain: Drive slowly and do not break the flow of traffic; four-wheel drive does not prevent skids.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: How far before turning or changing lanes does New York law require you to signal?
questions.explain: Signal at least 100 feet before a turn or lane change.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: When preparing to turn right, where should your vehicle be?
options: As far to the right as possible, then turn into the right lane
In the center of the lane
In the left lane to make a wide turn
questions.explain: Get as far right as possible, avoid wide sweeping turns, and turn into the right lane unless signs direct otherwise.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: Turning left from a one-way road onto a one-way road with two lanes, which lane should you turn into?
questions.explain: Use the left lane to prepare, and turn into the left lane of the road you enter.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: When turning left from a two-way road onto another two-way road, where should you end up?
options: In the left lane against traffic
Just to the right of the center line of the road you enter
questions.explain: Approach from the right half closest to the center and enter to the right of the center line, as close to it as possible.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: When turning left from a two-way road onto a one-way road, which lane should you turn into?
options: The right lane of the one-way road
The left lane of the one-way road
questions.explain: Approach from the right half closest to the center, turn before the center of the intersection, and enter the left lane.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: While waiting in an intersection to turn left, how should you keep your front wheels?
options: Straight, until you actually begin the turn
questions.explain: Keep wheels straight; if you are hit from behind with wheels turned, you could be pushed into oncoming traffic.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: From which position may you make a U-turn?
options: From the left portion of the lane nearest the center line
questions.explain: U-turns may be made only from the left part of the lane nearest the center line, never from the right lane.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'U-Turns'

questions.q: You may not make a U-turn where other drivers cannot see your vehicle from how far away in either direction?
questions.explain: U-turns are prohibited near hilltops, curves or other spots where you cannot be seen from 500 feet away.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'U-Turns'

questions.q: Where is a U-turn always illegal?
options: At an intersection with a green left-turn arrow (unless signed otherwise)
On a limited-access expressway, even using a crossover path
questions.explain: U-turns are never allowed on limited-access expressways; they are also illegal in NYC business districts, school zones and where signs prohibit them.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'U-Turns'

questions.q: What is the first step of a three-point turn?
options: Signal right, pull over to the right and stop
Turn sharply left from the center of the road
Back up toward the left curb
Stop in the middle of the road
questions.explain: Signal right, pull over and stop; then signal left, check traffic, and turn left across the road.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'U-Turns'

questions.q: Within how many feet of a railroad crossing on a two-way road is passing on the left prohibited?
questions.explain: You may not pass within 100 feet of a railroad crossing on a two-way roadway.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: You may not pass on the left if you cannot return to the right lane before an oncoming vehicle comes within:
questions.explain: Do not pass unless you can safely return before oncoming traffic is within 200 feet.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: Passing on the left is prohibited within 100 feet of which of these on a two-way road when your view is obstructed?
questions.explain: No passing within 100 feet of a bridge, tunnel or viaduct on a two-way road when your view is obstructed.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: When may you pass another vehicle on the right?
options: When the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and you can pass safely
Whenever the vehicle ahead is going below the limit
questions.explain: Passing on the right is allowed when the vehicle ahead turns left, or on roads with two or more lanes in your direction, if safe and not prohibited.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Right'

questions.q: A vehicle ahead has stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross. What should you do?
options: Pass it carefully on the left
Stop too — never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian
questions.explain: You must never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk to let a pedestrian cross.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass'

questions.q: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: As soon as your rear bumper clears its front bumper
When you have gone 50 feet past it
When you can see the front bumper of the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror
When the other driver flashes lights
questions.explain: Signal, check that you can see the passed car's front bumper in the inside mirror, and glance over your right shoulder before returning.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: Before changing lanes, why should you look over your shoulder?
options: Because mirrors are illegal to rely on
To check your blind spot, which mirrors do not show
questions.explain: Even well-adjusted mirrors leave blind spots; always glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or passing.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: Another vehicle is passing you on the left. What should you do?
options: Slow slightly and stay centered in your lane
Move to the left side of your lane
questions.explain: When being passed, reduce speed slightly and stay centered until the vehicle has safely passed.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'Being Passed'

questions.q: Many vehicles are passing you on the right. What should you do?
options: Speed up to keep up with them
Move into the right lane and let them pass on the left
Stay in your lane and ignore them
questions.explain: If many vehicles pass you on the right, move right and let them pass on the left.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'Being Passed'

questions.q: May you drive on the shoulder to pass a vehicle on the right?
options: Yes, if the shoulder is paved
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left
No, unless a sign allows it or a traffic officer directs you
questions.explain: You may not drive on or across the shoulder or edge line unless a sign allows it or an officer directs you.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Right'

questions.q: Your lane has a solid yellow center line on your side. May you pass?
options: Yes, if no cars are coming
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is slow
questions.explain: You may not pass on the left if your lane has a solid yellow center line.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass on the Left'

questions.q: When should you signal your exit from an expressway?
options: At least 100 feet before the exit ramp
Only once you are on the ramp
You do not need to signal
questions.explain: Get into the correct lane early and signal at least 100 feet before reaching the exit ramp.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Expressway Driving'

questions.q: You miss your exit on an expressway. What should you do?
options: Cross the median to turn around
Stop and wait for traffic to clear
questions.explain: Stay on the expressway until the next exit; backing up on a ramp or crossing a median is dangerous.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Expressway Driving'

questions.q: The expressway entrance lane is too short to reach highway speed. What is the safest way to enter?
options: Enter slowly and let others go around you
Drive onto the shoulder to build speed
Stop and wait for a large gap, then enter and accelerate quickly
Enter at whatever speed you have
questions.explain: If the entrance lane is too short, stop and wait for a large space in traffic, then enter and accelerate quickly.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Expressway Driving'

questions.q: Unless there is a STOP or YIELD sign or signal on the ramp, how should you use an expressway entrance ramp?
options: Stop at the end of the ramp
Drive slowly until a driver lets you in
Merge directly into the left lane
Accelerate to expressway speed and blend in with traffic
questions.explain: Use the ramp to build up to expressway speed, signal, check over your shoulder, and merge.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Expressway Driving'

questions.q: In a lane marked with arrows that curve to the right, what must you do?
options: Turn right — be in the correct lane before the solid line begins
Go straight or right as you choose
questions.explain: Pavement arrows show which lanes you must use; get in the correct lane before reaching the solid line separating lanes.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 4, 'Pavement Markings'

questions.q: How close may you park to a fire hydrant (unless a licensed driver stays in the vehicle)?
questions.explain: You may not park, stop or stand within 15 feet of a hydrant unless a licensed driver remains to move the vehicle.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: How close may you park or stand to a crosswalk at an intersection?
questions.explain: Parking or standing is not allowed within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: How close may you park to a traffic light, STOP sign or YIELD sign?
questions.explain: Parking or standing is not allowed within 30 feet of a traffic light, STOP sign or YIELD sign.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: How close may you park to a railroad crossing?
questions.explain: You may not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: How close may you park to a fire station driveway on the same side of the street?
questions.explain: No parking within 20 feet of a fire station driveway on the same side, or within 75 feet on the opposite side.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: Across the street from a fire station driveway, how far away must you park?
questions.explain: On the opposite side of the road, keep at least 75 feet from a fire station driveway.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: Unless another distance is marked, you may not park, stop or stand within how many feet of a pedestrian safety area?
questions.explain: Keep 30 feet from a pedestrian safety area unless a different distance is marked.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: After parallel parking, how close to the curb must your wheels be?
questions.explain: In the final position, your wheels must be no more than one foot from the curb.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'How to Park'

questions.q: When starting to parallel park, you stop beside the vehicle in front of the space. About how much space should be between the two vehicles?
questions.explain: Stop next to the vehicle ahead of the space, leaving about two feet between vehicles.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'How to Park'

questions.q: When parking on a hill, which is correct?
options: Leave the wheels straight and use the parking brake only
Put the car in neutral with the brake set
Set the parking brake, put the car in Park (or 1st gear), and turn the wheels so the car cannot roll into traffic
Turn the wheels toward the road
questions.explain: Apply the parking brake, select Park (1st gear in a manual car), and point the front wheels toward the curb or road edge so the car cannot roll out into traffic.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'How to Park on a Hill'

questions.q: What does a NO PARKING sign allow?
options: Stopping only to obey a traffic officer
A temporary stop to load or unload merchandise or passengers
questions.explain: At a NO PARKING sign you may stop temporarily to load or unload merchandise or passengers.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: What does a NO STANDING sign allow?
options: A temporary stop only to pick up or drop off passengers, without the driver leaving the vehicle
questions.explain: NO STANDING allows only a brief stop to load or discharge passengers; the driver may not leave the vehicle.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: What does a NO STOPPING sign mean?
options: Stop only to drop off passengers
Stop only to obey a sign, signal or officer, or to avoid a conflict with other vehicles
Stop for up to three minutes
questions.explain: At a NO STOPPING sign you may stop only to obey traffic controls or an officer, or to avoid conflicts with other vehicles.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed in New York, even briefly?
options: Parking 60 feet from a railroad crossing
Stopping on the road side of a parked vehicle (double parking)
Parking 35 feet from a STOP sign
questions.explain: You cannot park, stop or stand on the road side of a parked vehicle (double parking).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: May you park on a crosswalk in the middle of a block?
options: Yes, if it is not at an intersection
No — you may not park, stop or stand in any crosswalk
questions.explain: Parking, stopping or standing on a sidewalk or in a crosswalk is prohibited.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: Which of these is a place where you may NOT park, stop or stand?
options: On a bridge or in a tunnel
On a residential street with no signs
questions.explain: Parking, stopping and standing are prohibited on bridges, in tunnels, on railroad tracks, in intersections (unless permitted) and similar places.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Parking Regulations'

questions.q: May you park in the diagonally striped area next to a disability parking space?
options: No, it is needed for wheelchair and lift access
Yes, if you have a small car
Yes, if all other spaces are full
questions.explain: The striped access aisles next to reserved spaces must stay clear for wheelchairs and special equipment.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Reserved Parking for People with Disabilities'

questions.q: Unless a municipality sets higher penalties, what is the fine for a first-offense disability parking violation at a shopping center?
questions.explain: The fine is $50–$75 for a first offense ($75–$150 for a second within two years), plus a mandatory $30 surcharge.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'Reserved Parking for People with Disabilities'

questions.q: After you have parked on the street, when may you open the door on the traffic side?
options: Any time you need to get out
Only if the car is in a legal space
Only after turning on your flashers
Only when it will not interfere with bicyclists or other traffic
questions.explain: Do not open a road-side door if it would interfere with bicyclists or other traffic.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 7, 'How to Park'

questions.q: Children are nearby and you need to back out of a driveway. What should you do?
options: Get out and check behind the vehicle before backing
Rely on your backup camera only
Sound the horn and back quickly
Back out slowly using mirrors only
questions.explain: Before backing into or out of a driveway when children may be near, get out and check behind the vehicle.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When passing a motorcycle, how much room should you give it?
options: A full lane, just as for a car
Enough to share the lane if the motorcycle is to one side
questions.explain: Give motorcycles the same full-lane width as other vehicles; never share a lane with one.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass'

questions.q: How many motorcycles may ride side by side in a single lane in New York?
questions.explain: Two motorcyclists may ride side by side in one lane, but a motorcyclist may not share a lane with a car.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Motorcyclists'

questions.q: Most crashes between motorcycles and other vehicles happen because:
options: The other driver failed to see the motorcycle
questions.explain: Most motorcycle–vehicle crashes occur because the other driver did not see the motorcycle.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 5, 'Turns'

questions.q: Why might a motorcycle's turn signal be flashing even though the rider is not turning?
options: Many motorcycle signals do not turn off automatically
Riders use them to say hello
They flash to show the bike is slowing
questions.explain: Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so they may be left on by mistake; wait to see what the rider does.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Motorcyclists'

questions.q: When overtaking a bicyclist from behind, the law requires you to:
options: Pass on the left at a safe distance until you are clear of the bicycle
Stay behind until the cyclist turns off
questions.explain: Pass bicyclists on the left at a safe distance until clear; reduce speed, since your air pressure can unbalance them.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 6, 'How to Pass'

questions.q: Where must a bicyclist ride when there is no bicycle lane?
options: In the center of the lane
On the left side facing traffic
Near the right curb, road edge, or a usable right shoulder
questions.explain: Without a bike lane, cyclists stay near the right curb or edge (they may move left to turn or avoid hazards).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Bicyclists and their passengers of which ages must wear an approved helmet in New York?
questions.explain: Bicyclists and passengers ages 1–13 must wear approved helmets; adults follow local laws.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: A bicycle ridden at night must have a white headlight visible from at least how far ahead?
questions.explain: A night-time bicycle needs a headlight visible from 500 feet and a red taillight visible from 300 feet.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: What is the most bicyclists may ride side by side in a single lane?
questions.explain: Bicyclists must never ride more than two abreast in a single lane.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Before turning right on red, what should you check for bicyclists?
options: Nothing; bicycles must stop for you
Look to the right and behind for a cyclist coming up on your right rear
questions.explain: Stop fully and look left-right-left and behind to avoid hitting a cyclist approaching from the right rear.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Must bicyclists obey traffic signs and signals?
options: Yes, they have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers
questions.explain: Bicyclists must obey the rules of the road; drivers must also yield to them as they would to other vehicles.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Bicyclists'

questions.q: Where there are no sidewalks, pedestrians should walk:
options: Facing traffic, as far from the near lane as possible
In the center of the lane
questions.explain: Pedestrians must use the sidewalk when available, or walk facing traffic as far from the lane as possible.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: A large truck ahead signaling a right turn moves slightly to the left first. Why?
options: Trucks swing wide to make right turns
The truck is about to pass
questions.explain: Large vehicles make wide right turns and may move left first; do not squeeze in on the right.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: A tractor with a long hood can have a blind spot in front of it of about:
questions.explain: Long-hood tractors can have a 20-foot blind spot in front; avoid these 'no zones'.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: After passing a large truck, when may you move back in front of it?
options: Right after your rear bumper clears its cab
When the truck flashes its lights
When you can see the whole front of the truck in your rear-view mirror
questions.explain: Do not pull in front of a large vehicle until you can see its whole front in your mirror.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: A truck is backing up across the road into a loading area. What should you do?
questions.explain: Never pass close behind a backing large vehicle; you may be in its blind spot. Wait.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: You are stopped behind a truck facing uphill at a light. Why leave extra space?
options: The truck may roll back slightly when it starts
So the truck driver can see your plates
questions.explain: A truck or bus may roll back slightly when starting, especially uphill; leave room to pull around.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: Why does a tractor-trailer with air brakes take longer to stop than a car at the same speed?
options: Brake delay as air pressure is transmitted from tractor to trailer
questions.explain: Air brakes transmit braking from tractor to trailer, adding many feet to stopping distance.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: An approaching tractor-trailer on a two-way road often seems:
options: Exactly as fast as it is
Slower and smaller than it really is
questions.explain: A truck's large size makes it appear to move slower than it is, and from a distance it may not look as big as it is.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: In more than 60 percent of fatal crashes involving cars and big trucks:
options: The car driver contributes to the cause
The truck driver alone is at fault
Bad weather is the only cause
questions.explain: In over 60% of fatal car–truck crashes the car driver, not the truck driver, contributes to the cause.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Large Vehicles'

questions.q: What is illegal when you approach or pass a horse being ridden or led along a road?
questions.explain: It is illegal to sound your horn when approaching or passing a horse; drive at a careful speed and distance.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Horse Riders'

questions.q: Where may Class B and Class C mopeds be driven?
options: In the right-hand lane, as far right as possible (or the shoulder)
questions.explain: Class B and C mopeds must stay in the right lane as far right as possible; Class A may use any lane.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Moped Operators'

questions.q: Are mopeds allowed on expressways and other controlled-access highways?
options: Yes, Class A only, at any time
No, unless posted signs permit it
questions.explain: Mopeds may not use expressways or controlled-access highways unless signs allow it.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Moped Operators'

questions.q: Before crossing a highway, ATVs and snowmobiles must:
options: Stop, yield to traffic, and cross at a 90-degree angle
questions.explain: ATVs and snowmobiles must stop, yield, and cross at a right angle to the road.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'All-Terrain Vehicles and Snowmobiles'

questions.q: Which turning movement is involved in more than 35 percent of New York City pedestrian injury crashes?
options: Drivers making right turns on red
questions.explain: More than 35% of NYC pedestrian injury crashes occur when a driver is turning left.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: When turning right at an intersection, which pedestrians should you especially watch for?
options: Pedestrians on the far left corner only
None; they must wait for you
questions.explain: On right turns watch for pedestrians on your right; on left turns watch the crosswalk on the far side to your left.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 11, 'Pedestrians'

questions.q: New York is a 'primary enforcement' seat belt state. What does that mean?
options: Only the driver must buckle up
You can only be ticketed after another violation
Seat belts are optional on local roads
Police can stop you just because someone is not wearing a seat belt
questions.explain: Under primary enforcement, an officer can pull you over solely for a seat belt violation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: Who is responsible for making sure passengers under 16 are buckled up or in a proper child restraint?
questions.explain: The driver must ensure each passenger under 16 is restrained and faces a $25–$100 fine and 3 points per violation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: A child under age 4 must ride in:
options: A booster seat with a lap belt only
A federally approved child safety seat attached by a seat belt or LATCH
The front seat with an adult's lap
questions.explain: Children under 4 must be in a federally approved child safety seat attached with a seat belt or LATCH.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride rear-facing (unless they outgrow the seat's rear-facing limits)?
questions.explain: Children must ride rear-facing until age 2 or until they reach the seat's highest rear-facing weight or height limit.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: A child aged 4 through 7 must generally be restrained in:
options: Any seat belt, if seated in back
An appropriate child restraint such as a booster seat used with a lap and shoulder belt
questions.explain: Children 4–7 must use an appropriate approved child restraint (commonly a booster) with lap and shoulder belt; seat belts alone don't qualify.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: Passengers aged 8 through 15 must:
options: Wear a seat belt, one person per belt
questions.explain: Passengers 8–15 must be properly restrained by a seat belt, one person per belt.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: Where should you never place a rear-facing infant seat?
options: In the back seat behind the driver
In the front seat of a vehicle with a passenger air bag
In the middle of the back seat
questions.explain: Never put a rear-facing child seat in front of a passenger air bag.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: How far should the center of your chest be from the air bag cover in the steering wheel?
questions.explain: Sit with at least 10 inches between your chest and the air bag cover.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Seat Belts, Child Safety Seats, and Air Bags'

questions.q: In New York, is it legal to talk on a hand-held cell phone while driving?
options: Yes, if stopped at a red light
No — it is a traffic infraction; only hands-free use is allowed
questions.explain: Speaking into or listening to a hand-held phone while driving is an infraction (fine up to $200 and 5 points first offense). Hands-free phones may be used.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Using a Cellular or Mobile Telephone'

questions.q: What is the maximum fine for a first offense of texting while driving in New York?
questions.explain: Texting fines: up to $200 for a first offense, up to $250 for a second within 18 months, up to $450 for a third.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Using a Cellular or Mobile Telephone'

questions.q: On a long trip, how often should you plan a rest stop to prevent fatigue?
questions.explain: Schedule regular stops every 100 miles or two hours.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Drowsy and Fatigued Driving'

questions.q: You feel drowsy while driving. What is the best response?
options: Open the window and turn up the radio
Drive faster to get home sooner
Stop in a safe place; take a 15–45 minute nap and/or caffeine
questions.explain: Radio and open windows don't work; pull off safely, take a short nap, and caffeine (takes about 30 minutes to work) can help.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Drowsy and Fatigued Driving'

questions.q: An aggressive driver is following you. What should you do?
options: Brake suddenly to make them back off
Make eye contact so they know you see them
Do not stop or get out; drive to the nearest police station
questions.explain: Avoid eye contact, stay calm, move away, and if followed, drive to a police station without stopping.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Aggressive Drivers'

questions.q: When does New York law require headlights?
options: From a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, when visibility is under 1,000 feet, and when using wipers for weather
questions.explain: Headlights are required from ½ hour after sunset to ½ hour before sunrise, when visibility is under 1,000 feet, and whenever wipers are used for rain, snow or sleet.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: You must switch to low beams when an oncoming vehicle is within:
questions.explain: Use low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 200 feet of a vehicle you are following.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: You must use low beams when following another vehicle within:
questions.explain: Dim your lights within 200 feet of a vehicle ahead, even if it is in another lane.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: An oncoming vehicle's high beams are blinding you. Where should you look?
options: Toward the right edge of the road
questions.explain: Move your eyes to the right and use the road edge as a guide until the vehicle passes.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: Which headlight setting is best in fog, rain or falling snow?
questions.explain: High beams reflect off fog, rain and snow; low beams give better visibility.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving in Rain, Fog or Snow'

questions.q: What is hydroplaning?
options: Tires riding on a layer of water, losing traction and steering
questions.explain: In heavy rain tires can ride on water on the pavement, causing loss of traction and steering; slow down.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving in Rain, Fog or Snow'

questions.q: Which parts of the road freeze first in winter weather?
questions.explain: Bridges, ramps and overpasses freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: In New York, tires with metal studs may be used only:
questions.explain: Studded tires are allowed only from October 16 through April 30.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: When the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least how far from the nearest rail?
questions.explain: Stop at least 15 feet from the tracks and wait until the lights and bell stop and gates are fully up.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Railroad Crossing Signals'

questions.q: At a crossing with multiple tracks, a train has just passed. When may you cross?
options: As soon as the last car passes
When you can clearly see down all tracks in both directions and no other train is coming
questions.explain: Another train may be hidden; wait until you can see clearly down all tracks both ways.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Railroad Crossings'

questions.q: When may you drive onto railroad tracks at a crossing?
options: When traffic ahead is moving slowly
Only when there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side
When you can cross before the lights flash
questions.explain: Do not start across unless your whole vehicle will clear all the tracks.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Railroad Crossing Warning Sign'

questions.q: Which vehicles must stop at all railroad crossings, so you should be ready to stop behind them?
options: School buses, buses carrying passengers, and vehicles with explosives or flammable cargo
questions.explain: School buses (with or without passengers), other buses with passengers, and vehicles carrying explosives or flammable cargo must stop at all crossings.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Railroad Crossing Warning Sign'

questions.q: Your vehicle stalls on the railroad tracks. What is the first thing to do?
options: Get everyone out and away from the tracks
Call a tow truck from inside the car
Push the vehicle off the tracks
questions.explain: Get out immediately with all passengers, move away from the tracks, then call the number on the Emergency Notification System sign.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Stalling on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: If a train is approaching after you leave a stalled vehicle on the tracks, which way should you run?
options: Down the tracks in the same direction the train is going
Toward the train, away from the tracks at about a 45-degree angle
Straight along the tracks away from the train
questions.explain: Run toward the approaching train but away from the tracks at a 45° angle to avoid flying debris.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Stalling on Railroad Tracks'

questions.q: Two-thirds of deer–vehicle collisions in New York happen in which months?
questions.explain: Most deer crashes occur October–December, the breeding season; deer are most active at dawn and dusk.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Avoid Collisions With Deer'

questions.q: What is the minimum legal tire tread depth in New York?
questions.explain: Tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread; if you see all of Lincoln's head in the penny test, the tires are too worn.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Vehicle Condition'

questions.q: How should you brake on a slippery road in a car with anti-lock brakes (ABS)?
options: Keep firm, even pressure on the brake pedal
Release the brake and steer only
questions.explain: With ABS, keep steady pressure; without ABS, pump carefully.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: Your rear wheels start to skid to the left. Which way should you steer?
options: To the left — the direction the rear is sliding
questions.explain: Steer toward the direction the back of the car is sliding (the way the car is trying to go). If it then slides the other way, steer that way.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: If your front wheels skid, what should you do first?
options: Steer sharply in the direction you want to go
Take your foot off the gas and shift to neutral (or push in the clutch), without steering right away
questions.explain: Ease off the gas, shift to neutral, and wait for traction to return before steering.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'How to Drive in Winter'

questions.q: In a work zone with a 'lane closed ahead' sign, what should you do?
options: Speed to the end of the closed lane and cut in
Merge into the open lane as soon as it is safe
questions.explain: Merge early at first notice; racing to the end of the closed lane is unsafe.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'How to Drive Safely in Work Zones'

questions.q: What is the most common type of crash in highway work zones?
questions.explain: Rear-end crashes are most common in work zones; keep two seconds or more behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'How to Drive Safely in Work Zones'

questions.q: How do you exit a roundabout?
options: Turn on your right signal as you approach your exit and yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk
Stop in the circle to check traffic
questions.explain: Signal right as you near your exit and yield to pedestrians when exiting.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: Can you pass a bicycle inside a roundabout?
options: No, do not pass a bicycle in a roundabout
questions.explain: Cyclists ride in the lane like other vehicles; do not pass them within the roundabout.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Roundabouts'

questions.q: Which driver-assist features are NOT permitted during the New York road test?
options: Adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking
questions.explain: Adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking may not be used on the road test; warning systems like cameras are permitted.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 13, 'Vehicle Technologies Permitted and Not Permitted for Testing'

questions.q: How should you treat a driver approaching a STOP sign on a side road?
options: Assume they might not stop, and be ready to react
Speed up to pass the intersection first
questions.explain: Defensive drivers anticipate errors and assume the other driver may not stop or yield.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Be Prepared and Look Ahead'

questions.q: How can you reduce glare from the headlights of vehicles behind you at night?
options: Switch the inside rear-view mirror to its night position
questions.explain: Flip the inside mirror to 'night' and keep the dome light off and dash lights dim.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Night Driving'

questions.q: Which of these is a sign of drowsy driving?
options: Wanting to change the radio station
Drifting between lanes or hitting the rumble strips
questions.explain: Drifting, yawning, heavy eyelids, and not remembering the last few miles are warning signs of fatigue.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 8, 'Drowsy and Fatigued Driving'

questions.q: What is the most important rule in any driving emergency?
questions.explain: Keeping calm gives you the best chance; you usually have a second or two to think before acting.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: A front tire blows out. What should you do?
options: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and don't brake until the car is under control
questions.explain: Grip the wheel, let the car slow, avoid braking until controlled, then leave the road safely.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your steering suddenly stops responding. What should you do?
options: Slowly ease off the gas, turn on emergency flashers, and keep off the brake as long as it's safe
questions.explain: A sudden speed change could cause loss of control; let the vehicle slow, then brake very gently to stop.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your brake pedal suddenly sinks to the floor. What should you try first?
options: Pump the brake pedal to build pressure
questions.explain: Pump the pedal first; if that fails, apply the parking/emergency brake gradually and downshift.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your headlights suddenly go out at night. What should you try?
options: Your emergency flashers, parking lights and turn signals
questions.explain: Flashers, parking lights and turn signals may still work and give enough light to leave the road safely.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your gas pedal sticks. If you cannot free it with your shoe, what should you do?
options: Shift to neutral, brake, and pull off the road — but don't turn off the ignition
questions.explain: Turning off the ignition can lock the steering; shift to neutral and brake to a stop off the road.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your right wheels drift off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?
options: Jerk the wheel to get back on quickly
Ease off the gas, brake gently, and steer back on carefully after slowing and checking traffic
questions.explain: Don't swerve back; slow down first, check traffic, then return carefully.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: A vehicle is coming head-on toward you in your lane. What should you do?
options: Slow down, pull to the right, and sound your horn
questions.explain: Do not turn left — the other driver may swerve back into their lane, causing a head-on crash.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: Your car goes into water. How should you escape?
options: Wait for the car to sink completely
Stay inside and call for help
Unbuckle and get out through a window
questions.explain: An open door lets water rush in and the car could roll; escape through a window. If it sinks first, move to the back seat air pocket.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: You see smoke coming from under the hood. What should you do?
options: Pull off, turn off the ignition, get away from the car, and call the fire department
Open the hood and fight the fire
Keep driving to a service station
questions.explain: It is dangerous to fight a vehicle fire yourself.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'

questions.q: If you are involved in a crash, when must you stop?
options: Always, regardless of the amount of damage
questions.explain: You must stop at any crash; leaving the scene is a violation (property damage) or a crime (injury or death).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'At the Scene'

questions.q: Leaving the scene of a crash that caused personal injury or death is:
options: A traffic infraction with a small fine
Legal if your car is undamaged
questions.explain: Leaving the scene of an injury or fatal crash is a criminal violation and also carries mandatory licence revocation.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'At the Scene'

questions.q: When must a crash be reported to the DMV?
options: Within 24 hours, only if police came
Only if your insurer requests it
Within 10 days, if anyone was injured or killed or damage to any one person's property is $1,000 or more
questions.explain: File an MV-104 within 10 days for injury/death or $1,000+ damage to one person's property.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'Reports to DMV'

questions.q: Failing to report a reportable crash to the DMV is:
options: A misdemeanor that can lead to license suspension or revocation
Not a problem if you told your insurance company
questions.explain: Reporting to your insurer does not satisfy the requirement; failing to report is a criminal offense (misdemeanor).
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'Reports to DMV'

questions.q: You damage an unattended parked car. What must you do?
options: Try to find the owner or notify the police
questions.explain: If a parked vehicle or other property is damaged, try to locate the owner or notify the police.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'At the Scene'

questions.q: At a crash scene, when should you move an injured person?
options: Only if necessary because of fire or other life-threatening danger
questions.explain: Do not move the injured unless fire or another life-threatening danger makes it necessary; keep the back and neck straight if you must.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'Emergency First-Aid'

questions.q: Power lines are down on a crashed vehicle. What should the occupants do?
options: Touch the wires to move them
questions.explain: Do not go near downed wires; if they touch or lie near the vehicle, occupants should remain inside.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'Emergency First-Aid'

questions.q: After a crash involving only property damage, what information must you exchange?
options: Name, address, license number, registration and insurance information
questions.explain: Exchange name, address, licence number, registration and insurance information (policy number and effective date) with the other drivers.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'At the Scene'

questions.q: If someone is injured in a crash, what must happen?
options: Wait to see if they feel better
Police must be notified immediately and ambulance help called
Drive them to a hospital before calling anyone
questions.explain: If anyone is hurt or killed, notify police immediately and make sure an ambulance or rescue has been called.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 12, 'At the Scene'

questions.q: Your car stalls on railroad tracks with no train in sight. After confirming no train is coming, what may you do?
options: Stay in the car and wait for help
Leave the car on the tracks and walk home
Open your window to listen, try to restart, and if that fails, shift to neutral and push it off
Keep cranking the engine without checking for trains
questions.explain: Only when you are completely sure no train is coming, listen and try to restart; otherwise push the vehicle off in neutral.
questions.ref: New York State Driver's Manual (MV-21, 2026 PDF), Chapter 10, 'Driving Emergencies'
